security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences or command examples, not executable skill code. No prompt injection or data exfiltration intent was found. A medium semantic issue remains because several examples combine public network binding with reload or development-oriented settings without a clear warning.

remediation.issue: Public bind examples are shown with reload-enabled settings.
remediation.suggestion: Add a warning to prefer localhost for development and avoid reload on public interfaces.

remediation.issue: Command examples could be copied into production without context.
remediation.suggestion: Label examples by environment and state which options are development-only.

remediation.issue: TLS key and certificate paths are shown without handling guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend strict key file permissions and environment-specific secret management.

semantic_findings.title: Public Reload Server Exposure
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md combines bind-all interface examples with reload-enabled Uvicorn configurations. Users who copy these examples can expose a development server to a network.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited examples directly pair 0.0.0.0 binding with reload-enabled development settings. The risk is operational guidance rather than automatic code execution, so medium severity is appropriate.

content.value_statement: ASGI server setup can be confusing across local, Docker, and production environments. This skill gives concise Uvicorn patterns for startup, workers, TLS, sockets, and troubleshooting.
actual_capabilities: Shows basic Uvicorn startup commands with host, port, and reload options.
Provides simple ASGI and FastAPI application examples.
Explains factory app startup and programmatic Uvicorn server control.
Covers workers, Gunicorn integration, TLS flags, Unix sockets, and Docker examples.
Lists common CLI flags and troubleshooting checks.
limitations: It is a documentation guide and does not install or run Uvicorn by itself.
It does not validate the user application import path or dependency versions.
It does not replace production hardening for proxies, TLS, secrets, or access controls.
Examples need environment-specific review before use on public networks.

use_cases.title: Start a FastAPI app locally
use_cases.description: Use the guide to choose host, port, reload, and application module settings for a local ASGI app.

use_cases.title: Prepare a production server command
use_cases.description: Select worker, process manager, logging, and TLS options before deploying an ASGI service.

use_cases.title: Containerize an ASGI service
use_cases.description: Map Uvicorn startup choices into Dockerfile and Compose service settings.

prompt_templates.title: Start a local app
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the uvicorn skill to help me run a FastAPI app from main:app with reload on a local development port.

prompt_templates.title: Select server options
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my ASGI app requirements and recommend Uvicorn host, port, reload, workers, and log settings with rationale.

prompt_templates.title: Plan production deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the uvicorn skill to design a Gunicorn plus Uvicorn worker setup for this app, including worker count and logging choices.

prompt_templates.title: Harden container startup
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Docker Compose service for Uvicorn and suggest safer networking, reload, volume, health check, and process settings.

output_examples.input: I need to run a new FastAPI app locally.
output_examples.output: The response identifies the application target, recommends localhost with reload, confirms the port, and flags public binding as a separate choice.

output_examples.input: I need a production command for four workers.
output_examples.output: The response compares direct Uvicorn workers with a Gunicorn process manager and explains when reload should stay disabled.

output_examples.input: My Docker Compose Uvicorn service reloads on every change.
output_examples.output: The response checks mounted paths, reload scope, port exposure, and whether the service is intended for development.

best_practices: Use localhost for development unless a network-accessible server is required.
Keep reload enabled only for development and disable it for production workers.
Protect TLS key files with strict permissions and environment-specific secret handling.
anti_patterns: Binding a reload-enabled development server to all interfaces without access controls.
Using reload and multiple workers together in the same production command.
Committing local certificate keys or environment-specific port settings to shared templates.

faq.question: Does this skill run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents commands and configuration patterns that the user or agent must choose to run.

faq.question: Which frameworks does it support?
faq.answer: It covers Uvicorn usage for ASGI applications such as FastAPI, Starlette, Django Channels, and WebSocket services.

faq.question: Can it help with production deployment?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes worker options, Gunicorn integration, Docker examples, TLS flags, and operational troubleshooting notes.

faq.question: Does it replace Uvicorn documentation?
faq.answer: No. It is a concise workflow guide and should be paired with official docs for version-specific details.

faq.question: Is binding to all network interfaces always safe?
faq.answer: No. Use it only when the service needs network access and has appropriate firewall and authentication controls.

faq.question: Can I use reload in production?
faq.answer: Reload is intended for development. Production deployments should use stable worker processes without live reload.
